if reverse:
        agg = agg[::-1]

    if subset_rank_limit is not None:
        # Determine whether to take head or tail based on sort_by
        if sort_by == 'degree':
            # Assume query returns ascending degree; we want highest degree -> take tail
            agg_slice = agg.iloc[-subset_rank_limit:]
            # Compute offset of first kept row
            start_idx = len(agg) - subset_rank_limit
        else:
            agg_slice = agg.iloc[:subset_rank_limit]
            start_idx = 0
        agg = agg_slice
        # Keep rows where _bin falls within kept slice
        keep_mask = (df["_bin"] >= start_idx) & (df["_bin"] < start_idx + subset_rank_limit)
        df = df[keep_mask].copy()
        # Remap _bin to new sequential order
        df["_bin"] = df["_bin"].map({old: new - start_idx for new, old in enumerate(range(start_idx, start_idx + subset_rank_limit))})

    return results.total, df, agg, results.category_totals
